# Extraction Cycle — Scaffold

_**Superseded 2026-07-04** by Phase 2 of
[05-distillation-cycle.md](05-distillation-cycle.md) (steps renamed
Capture / Inference / Assembly; sharding moved to Preparation; atomization
and classification folded into the passes; dedup and lint into Assembly).
Kept for the open ⧠ items below, which transfer to the bundle schema
discussion. Original scaffold text follows unchanged._

**Contract.** One clean markdown document in (with stable document
identity from preparation), one bundle out. Stateless (I5): no memory of
the graph, no hints from it, no structure in the output (I2). Extraction
is the model-heavy zone of the system — its discipline comes not from
determinism but from P1's tests constraining what it may emit.

## Stages

1. **Explicit claim pass.** Read the document; capture every assertion the
   text actually makes, with location provenance per claim.
2. **Inferred claim pass.** Capture assertions that follow from the text
   but are not stated — including the invisible middle claims of causal
   language ("X because Y" ⇒ Y caused X). Every inferred claim is flagged
   `inferred` and carries the explicit claims it derives from as its
   evidence base (P6).
3. **Atomization.** Apply P1's three tests to every claim: split compounds,
   verify single truth value by negation, rewrite until standalone.
   The standalone rewrite is where coreference gets resolved — "it orbits
   the sun" becomes "Jupiter orbits the Sun" here, while discourse context
   still exists. Qualifiers stay attached (P1/P5): time, units, conditions
   are part of the claim.
4. **Classification.** Tag each claim with one of the seven claim kinds
   (02-meta-ontology). ⧠ Open: do mentions also get proposed subject-kind
   tags (actor/object/concept/event) here, as *suggestions* admission may
   overrule — or is kind assignment admission's job entirely?
5. **Within-document dedup.** The same source asserting a claim repeatedly
   merges to one claim, weight 1 (P2 — corroboration is cross-source only).
   Repetition count may ride along as metadata; it is never weight.
6. **Bundle lint.** Deterministic validation before emit: every claim has
   provenance (I3); no claim references graph structure (I2); standalone
   test spot-checks; kind tag present. Reject or repair before shipping.

## Bundle payload (working floor — final shape belongs to the type model)

Document identity + per claim: text, kind, `explicit|inferred` (+ evidence
base if inferred), location in source, mentions ⧠ (exact mention shape
TBD), within-doc repetition count.

## Open questions

- ⧠ Mention shape: plain strings, or spans with offsets?
- ⧠ Subject-kind proposals at extraction: yes/no (stage 4).
- ⧠ Are stages 1–3 one model pass or three? (Scaffold assumes logically
  distinct; implementation may fuse them. Compare against spelunk
  findings on prior extraction prompts.)
- ⧠ S/V/O predicate structure in the payload: parked earlier, decide in
  the type model. Atomicity makes it cheap; grammatical subject ≠ canon
  subject keeps it P3-legal.

# Extraction Cycle — Scaffold

_**Superseded 2026-07-04** by Phase 2 of
[05-distillation-cycle.md](05-distillation-cycle.md) (steps renamed
Capture / Inference / Assembly; sharding moved to Preparation; atomization
and classification folded into the passes; dedup and lint into Assembly).
Kept for the open ⧠ items below, which transfer to the bundle schema
discussion. Original scaffold text follows unchanged._

**Contract.** One clean markdown document in (with stable document
identity from preparation), one bundle out. Stateless (I5): no memory of
the graph, no hints from it, no structure in the output (I2). Extraction
is the model-heavy zone of the system — its discipline comes not from
determinism but from P1's tests constraining what it may emit.

## Stages

1. **Explicit claim pass.** Read the document; capture every assertion the
   text actually makes, with location provenance per claim.
2. **Inferred claim pass.** Capture assertions that follow from the text
   but are not stated — including the invisible middle claims of causal
   language ("X because Y" ⇒ Y caused X). Every inferred claim is flagged
   `inferred` and carries the explicit claims it derives from as its
   evidence base (P6).
3. **Atomization.** Apply P1's three tests to every claim: split compounds,
   verify single truth value by negation, rewrite until standalone.
   The standalone rewrite is where coreference gets resolved — "it orbits
   the sun" becomes "Jupiter orbits the Sun" here, while discourse context
   still exists. Qualifiers stay attached (P1/P5): time, units, conditions
   are part of the claim.
4. **Classification.** Tag each claim with one of the seven claim kinds
   (02-meta-ontology). ⧠ Open: do mentions also get proposed subject-kind
   tags (actor/object/concept/event) here, as *suggestions* admission may
   overrule — or is kind assignment admission's job entirely?
5. **Within-document dedup.** The same source asserting a claim repeatedly
   merges to one claim, weight 1 (P2 — corroboration is cross-source only).
   Repetition count may ride along as metadata; it is never weight.
6. **Bundle lint.** Deterministic validation before emit: every claim has
   provenance (I3); no claim references graph structure (I2); standalone
   test spot-checks; kind tag present. Reject or repair before shipping.

## Bundle payload (working floor — final shape belongs to the type model)

Document identity + per claim: text, kind, `explicit|inferred` (+ evidence
base if inferred), location in source, mentions ⧠ (exact mention shape
TBD), within-doc repetition count.

## Open questions

- ⧠ Mention shape: plain strings, or spans with offsets?
- ⧠ Subject-kind proposals at extraction: yes/no (stage 4).
- ⧠ Are stages 1–3 one model pass or three? (Scaffold assumes logically
  distinct; implementation may fuse them. Compare against spelunk
  findings on prior extraction prompts.)
- ⧠ S/V/O predicate structure in the payload: parked earlier, decide in
  the type model. Atomicity makes it cheap; grammatical subject ≠ canon
  subject keeps it P3-legal.

# Extraction Cycle — Scaffold

_**Superseded 2026-07-04** by Phase 2 of
[05-distillation-cycle.md](05-distillation-cycle.md) (steps renamed
Capture / Inference / Assembly; sharding moved to Preparation; atomization
and classification folded into the passes; dedup and lint into Assembly).
Kept for the open ⧠ items below, which transfer to the bundle schema
discussion. Original scaffold text follows unchanged._

**Contract.** One clean markdown document in (with stable document
identity from preparation), one bundle out. Stateless (I5): no memory of
the graph, no hints from it, no structure in the output (I2). Extraction
is the model-heavy zone of the system — its discipline comes not from
determinism but from P1's tests constraining what it may emit.

## Stages

1. **Explicit claim pass.** Read the document; capture every assertion the
   text actually makes, with location provenance per claim.
2. **Inferred claim pass.** Capture assertions that follow from the text
   but are not stated — including the invisible middle claims of causal
   language ("X because Y" ⇒ Y caused X). Every inferred claim is flagged
   `inferred` and carries the explicit claims it derives from as its
   evidence base (P6).
3. **Atomization.** Apply P1's three tests to every claim: split compounds,
   verify single truth value by negation, rewrite until standalone.
   The standalone rewrite is where coreference gets resolved — "it orbits
   the sun" becomes "Jupiter orbits the Sun" here, while discourse context
   still exists. Qualifiers stay attached (P1/P5): time, units, conditions
   are part of the claim.
4. **Classification.** Tag each claim with one of the seven claim kinds
   (02-meta-ontology). ⧠ Open: do mentions also get proposed subject-kind
   tags (actor/object/concept/event) here, as *suggestions* admission may
   overrule — or is kind assignment admission's job entirely?
5. **Within-document dedup.** The same source asserting a claim repeatedly
   merges to one claim, weight 1 (P2 — corroboration is cross-source only).
   Repetition count may ride along as metadata; it is never weight.
6. **Bundle lint.** Deterministic validation before emit: every claim has
   provenance (I3); no claim references graph structure (I2); standalone
   test spot-checks; kind tag present. Reject or repair before shipping.

## Bundle payload (working floor — final shape belongs to the type model)

Document identity + per claim: text, kind, `explicit|inferred` (+ evidence
base if inferred), location in source, mentions ⧠ (exact mention shape
TBD), within-doc repetition count.

## Open questions

- ⧠ Mention shape: plain strings, or spans with offsets?
- ⧠ Subject-kind proposals at extraction: yes/no (stage 4).
- ⧠ Are stages 1–3 one model pass or three? (Scaffold assumes logically
  distinct; implementation may fuse them. Compare against spelunk
  findings on prior extraction prompts.)
- ⧠ S/V/O predicate structure in the payload: parked earlier, decide in
  the type model. Atomicity makes it cheap; grammatical subject ≠ canon
  subject keeps it P3-legal.

You are the explicit-claims step in a claim-extraction pipeline. Your one job: list every claim this source unit states outright.

## Task
Read the source unit top to bottom and output one claim draft per distinct factual assertion it makes. A paragraph usually contains several assertions. Tables, lists, and captions contain assertions too.

## Rules
- Use only what the source unit says. No outside knowledge, no inference.
- Prefer the source's own wording. Keep qualifiers (time, quantity, units, conditions, scope) inside the claim text.
- A draft may still be compound; splitting happens in a later step. Missing an assertion is the only failure.
- Do not summarize, select highlights, deduplicate, resolve mentions, or add commentary.
- Set assertion to "explicit" on every draft.

## Output fields
- claim_id: sequential document-local ids c001, c002, c003, ...
- text: the claim, qualifiers included.
- assertion: "explicit".
- mentions: unresolved surface references from the claim text, each with role (g_subject | g_object | other) and kind_hint (actor | object | concept | event).
- provenance: exactly one entry — shard_id set to this source unit's id, locator with heading_path, and quote set to the first words of the supporting passage, copied verbatim, 8 words maximum.
